Scientific answer and scope

The information supplied does not determine a universal best addition temperature or a number of seconds. A useful conditional prediction is: add the salt immediately, at the supplied 20 degrees C (elapsed time zero), if it is cool salt with nonnegative dissolution energy cost, and the additive-capacity, constant-heater, linear-loss model below applies. Immediate addition is a global weak minimum in that model; this theorem does not assert a unique optimum or a measured time saving. The parameters are symbolic, not fitted. Neither the observations nor the formal check establish that these assumptions describe this particular pot and salt.

This revision addresses the human rejection recorded on 2026-11-17: the earlier model left the before/after net powers P,Q independent. That proof was mathematically verified but scientifically rejected. Its files are preserved in history/cycle1/, and its raw checks remain under checks/. The new model replaces independent stage powers with ONE shared temperature-dependent energy-transfer law, derives the power change on adding salt, and uses the resulting relationship throughout the heating trajectories to optimize timing. This is a change of model, not a new interpretation of the old theorem. No operator response has been requested or invented; incorporated_inputs is empty. No experiment was performed.

Supplied information versus additional choices

Supplied: 1 litre of water at 20 degrees C, in a pot on a stove; salt will be added. Salt amount, identity beyond 'salt', salt temperature, pot properties, heater and room conditions have not been specified. There are no heating curves or heat-flow observations. The volume alone does not determine the water-plus-pot heat capacity. It is not converted into an invented exact capacity or mass.

Chosen deterministic physical model: treat water and pot as one well-mixed thermal body initially at 20 degrees C. C>0 is their constant combined heat capacity (J/K). Add a fixed quantity of completely soluble salt with initial temperature Ts, the same across schedules. Assume Ts <= 20 degrees C for the reported minimum. Approximate the extra sensible heat capacity by S>=0 and the final solution-plus-pot capacity by C+S. Use a constant dissolution energy cost H>=0 (joules, positive for heat absorbed). These are independent calorimetric approximations. In particular S is an additive effective increment; S>=0 is NOT inferred from the volume or established as an exact property of real brine. Temperature-dependent solution heat capacities and dissolution enthalpies can invalidate these approximations. The sign and constancy of H over the heating range are hypotheses, not conclusions drawn from the word 'salt'. No numerical thermochemical values are imported from literature.

Assume instantaneous mixing and complete dissolution, no pause in heater input, no material loss or evaporation, and no phase changes before the endpoint. The mixture must remain liquid and the salt quantity must be soluble. Compare a fixed final composition and pressure, hence a fixed final solution boiling temperature B, left unknown. Boiling means first arrival of the mixed salted solution at this equilibrium temperature, not transient bubbles. Feasible addition temperatures are below the pure-water boiling point (unless salting at its onset). The mathematical comparison is proved on the larger interval [20,B], so it holds on this physical subset whenever the model applies; it does not authorize prolonged unsalted boiling or ignore evaporation occurring there.

The heater supplies constant thermal power W to the body. Heat loss to a room at fixed temperature A is k(T-A), with k>0 in W/K. The same W and k apply before and after salting, with no direct concentration dependence at a common temperature. Thus the physical law is
  capacity * dT/dt = N(T),     N(T) = W - k(T-A).
This represents a constant-input stove and an effective Newton cooling loss. A linear loss is a tractable approximation motivated by convective/conductive heat transfer, not an exact law for an evaporating pot over an arbitrary temperature range. Radiation, changes of surface area, salt suppression of evaporation, heater controls, and concentration-dependent transfer are omitted. These may matter in an actual apparatus. W is heater-to-system input, not electrical/gas rating. The formal result needs the combined reachability condition N(B)>0; it does not fit W,k,A separately. With k>0 this implies positive net heating at every modeled temperature below B.

Observation/inference model: there are no stochastic observations or empirical parameter estimates, so no likelihood or prior is introduced. A deterministic first-law model gives conditional predictions. The initial condition sets the integration origin; it does not estimate C,S,H,Ts,W,k,A or B. Measurements of heating curves, salt quantity and temperature, mixing cooling, and final boiling temperature would be needed to calibrate and test this family. In particular a before/after heating-rate measurement must account for the changed heat capacity to infer net power. Until such evidence exists, the conclusion is conditional rather than a universal kitchen timing rule.

Physical inference and its Lean translation

All five public definitions are scientifically necessary, with temperatures in degrees C, elapsed times in seconds, capacities in J/K and powers in watts:
  initialTemperature = 20.
  netPower W k A T = N(T) = W-k(T-A).
  mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = z(x) = (C*x + S*Ts-H)/(C+S).
  heatingTime capacity W k A u v = capacity/k * [ln N(u)-ln N(v)].
  boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x = t(x)
      = heatingTime C W k A 20 x
        + heatingTime (C+S) W k A z(x) B.
The logarithm difference is equivalently ln[N(u)/N(v)], a dimensionless ratio of powers; the formalization uses fixed SI numerical values. No logarithm of nonpositive power is used in the applicable domain.

The mixing formula follows from sensible energy and dissolution conservation:
  (C+S)*z = C*x + S*Ts-H.
This equation includes heating the added salt and paying dissolution energy. The lemma mixing_balance verifies it. Applying the SHARED heat-loss law at the two temperatures yields the derived relationship (power_change):
  N(z(x))-N(x) = k * [S*(x-Ts)+H]/(C+S).
For Ts<=20<=x, S,H>=0 the right side is nonnegative. Thus net heating power immediately after mixing is at least its value immediately before mixing. This comes from a reduced liquid temperature and hence reduced losses; the model does not increase the heater input or heat-transfer coefficient. At a common temperature the power is the same before and after salt addition. Increased net power does not by itself imply an increased temperature rate, because heat capacity has also changed. The proof compares the full times.

To derive stage times, invert the first law on a strictly heating stage:
  df/dT = capacity/N(T),    f(u)=0.
The lemma heating_time_derivative checks that heatingTime has exactly this derivative. The lemma stage_time_from_energy proves that ANY differentiable inverse elapsed-time curve satisfying that energy law on [u,v] and the zero initial condition has endpoint f(v)=heatingTime(...,u,v). It proves uniqueness by applying the mean-value monotonicity theorem to the difference and its negative. Thus the logarithmic time is derived from the energy equation rather than fitted or assumed as a timing optimum. Endpoint derivatives in that lemma are understood using smooth local extensions, possible when net power is strictly positive. For the two stages the capacities are C and C+S and the endpoints are (20,x) and (z(x),B). Their times add because mixing is instantaneous. This justifies boilingTime as the first-arrival time in this deterministic model.

Differentiating the full time, boiling_time_derivative proves
  dt/dx = C/N(x) - C/N(z(x)).
The power_order lemma derives 0 < N(x) <= N(z(x)) from the common heater/loss law and mixing balance under the stated hypotheses. It follows that dt/dx >= 0 throughout [20,B]. The final proof uses the mean-value monotonicity theorem to conclude t(20)<=t(x) for every admissible later addition. This accounts for subsequent temperature-dependent power; it does not replace it by an independent constant Q. Also heatingTime(C,...,20,20)=0, so the minimizing temperature corresponds to adding at elapsed time zero.

Exact final conclusion and compact review boundary

The sole submitted conclusion is the top-level theorem addition_timing_answer. For every C,S,H,Ts,B,W,k,A,x satisfying
  C>0; S>=0; H>=0; Ts<=initialTemperature;
  k>0; netPower W k A B>0; initialTemperature<=x<=B,
it proves the conjunction:
  N(z(x))-N(x) = k*[S*(x-Ts)+H]/(C+S);
  N(x)<=N(z(x));
  boilingTime(...,20)<=boilingTime(...,x);
  heatingTime(C,...,20,20)=0.
The first identity exposes the requested derived change in net heating power. The last two statements answer the temperature/time choice: now at 20 degrees C is no slower than a later feasible addition, within this model. Weak inequality is deliberate; no strictness or magnitude is inferred.

messages.content: The earlier assumption \(S\ge0\) is unjustified: \(S\) must represent the solution’s total heat capacity minus that of the original water, not just the solid salt’s heat capacity. I’ll allow either sign while requiring \(C+S>0\). I’ll also define dissolution energy at the salt’s initial temperature. The revised model gives conditional timing regimes—earliest, latest, an interior temperature, or a comparison of the endpoints—rather than a universal “add now” recommendation.

/usr/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
p='Model.lean'
s=open(p).read().split('/- Positive net power up to B,')[0]
s=s.replace('S the additional capacity, Ts salt temperature, H dissolution\\n   energy absorbed.', 'S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),\\n   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts.')
s=s.replace('/- Derive the mixing balance rather than assuming a cooling amount. -/', '''/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY"

/usr/bin/bash -lc "cat >> Model.lean <<'EOF'
/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).neg.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).neg.hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      have hn : C * (k * (S * (y - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
          (netPower W k A y * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) ≤ 0 :=
        div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
          (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hC)
            (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
              (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
          (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr hn
  have hh := hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv
  linarith

/- Conditional scientific answer over an explicitly feasible interval.
   S>=0: earliest, latest, or interior root as D changes sign.
   S<=0: compare endpoint boiling times. S=H=0: all schedules tie.
   H is allowed either sign; mixing need not cool or increase net power. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    x ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ S * (L - Ts) + H →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → S * (U - Ts) + H ≤ 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 < S → Ts - H / S ∈ Set.Icc L U →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A (Ts - H / S) ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S ≤ 0 →
      min (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L) (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U) ≤
        boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S = 0 → H = 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L = boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hx
  have hp : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc L U, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) := by
    intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y
      hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy).2.2
  have inc : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_increasing_on_cooling C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  have dec : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_decreasing_on_warming C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hS hD
    apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hD
    apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  · intro hS hr
    have hroot : S * ((Ts - H / S) - Ts) + H = 0 := by
      field_simp
      <;> ring
    by_cases hxr : x ≤ Ts - H / S
    · apply dec x (Ts - H / S) hx.1 hr.2 hxr
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply inc (Ts - H / S) x hr.1 hx.2 (le_of_not_ge hxr)
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS
    by_cases hD : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H
    · apply le_trans (min_le_left _ _)
      apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply le_trans (min_le_right _ _)
      apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
      intro y hy
      have hh := le_of_not_ge hD
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hH
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
    · apply dec L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
EOF
source /work/lean-env.sh
which lean
lean Model.lean > diagnostics/cycle3-compile-1.log 2>&1"

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),
   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The initial cooling and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →

  S = final solution capacity - original water capacity.
The pot contribution cancels in S. S is a signed effective capacity difference, NOT the positive capacity of the solid salt. We impose no sign on S. This is the requested conditional-regimes approach, not an assertion of a sign for all NaCl solutions or any other unspecified salt. For a specified solute with amount n, the thermodynamic definition gives S=n*C_app, where C_app is its apparent molar heat capacity at the specified composition and temperature. That apparent capacity is not the solid's molar capacity. A real solution's S(T) can vary with temperature; the constant-capacity approximation must be tested over the heating range.

Partanen & Partanen, Journal of Solution Chemistry 54, 286-316 (2025), Eq. (9), defines C_app as (solution capacity - pure-water capacity)/solute amount. Their analysis treats its composition and temperature dependence and distinguishes real apparent quantities from relative apparent quantities. This supports the capacity interpretation, not a constant value or sign for the user's water. We import no table values or parameter estimates.
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10953-024-01412-5

Dissolution energy reference and mixing balance

H (joules) is the integral isothermal enthalpy of dissolution of the fixed solid salt amount into the fixed water amount at temperature Ts, the ACTUAL initial salt temperature, with the chosen final concentration. Positive H means endothermic at that reference. H can have either sign. It is a fixed reference enthalpy, not a temperature-independent dissolution enthalpy at every addition temperature.

Take the original water-plus-pot enthalpy as zero at Ts and the separate salt's enthalpy as zero at its initial Ts. Under the constant-capacity model, the final solution-plus-pot enthalpy at temperature z is H+(C+S)*(z-Ts). Initial enthalpy just before addition at temperature x is C*(x-Ts). Instantaneous adiabatic mixing/dissolution therefore gives
  H+(C+S)*(z-Ts) = C*(x-Ts),
  z(x) = (C*x+S*Ts-H)/(C+S).
Equivalently, the signed mixing cooling energy is D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H, and z-x=-D(x)/(C+S). Negative D means WARMING on mixing; no cooling premise is used.

For consistency, if the solid salt's constant sensible capacity is cs, isothermal dissolution at x costs H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts). This follows by subtracting the reactant capacity C+cs from product capacity C+S and integrating the enthalpy slope. Warming the solid from Ts to x costs cs*(x-Ts); the sum is H+S*(x-Ts). The Lean lemma reference_consistent_balance proves that the resulting balance (C+S)*(z-x)+cs*(x-Ts)+H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts)=0 is equivalent to the displayed z(x). Thus a positive solid heat capacity does not force S>=0. cs cancels and is not an independent parameter needed by the timing conclusion. These affine enthalpy laws are modeling choices; the algebraic consequence is proved. Temperature-dependent capacities would require integrating their actual functions.

Partanen & Partanen, Journal of Solution Chemistry 52, 1352-1385 (2023), Section 2, treats apparent enthalpy, dissolution and adiabatic temperature changes with explicit reference quantities. It provides general thermodynamic background only, not evidence for this pot's H or an exact constant-capacity law.
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10953-023-01322-y

Heating law and feasible timing domain

The retained approximation is constant heater-to-body power W and fixed room temperature A, with the SAME Newtonian heat loss k*(T-A) before and after addition, k>0. Hence net power is N(T)=W-k*(T-A). Salt does not change W or k at a common temperature in this approximation. The energy law is capacity*dT/dt=N(T), with capacity C before addition and C+S afterward. This model omits evaporation, radiation beyond the effective linear approximation, changes in heat transfer with concentration, heater feedback, material loss, stirring delay and dissolution delay. Mixing and complete dissolution are instantaneous with no heater pause. These are exposed approximations, not inferred facts about the apparatus.

B0 denotes the unsalted boiling temperature and B the fixed final mixture boiling temperature, both at the chosen pressure. F is a common SAFE liquid lower bound for both compositions over the applicable trajectories (choose it within the liquid region, not below either freezing boundary). L and U bound the interval of feasible addition temperatures. The final theorem requires:
  F <= 20 <= L <= U <= B0;
  F <= z(L) and z(U) <= B;
  N(U)>0 and N(B)>0;
  C>0, C+S>0, k>0.
The assumptions do not allow waiting through unsalted boiling. U=B0 permits adding at its onset, without dwelling there. Similarly z(U)=B permits the final endpoint to occur on mixing, without an intervening boiling/evaporation stage. If strict pre-boiling addition is required and U=B0 is excluded, a latest-endpoint optimum becomes an infimum approached from below, unless a smaller closed operational upper bound is selected.

The lemma feasible_trajectory derives that z is increasing (slope C/(C+S)>0) irrespective of S's sign. Therefore every x in [L,U] satisfies 20<=x<=B0 and F<=z(x)<=B, and both stages have positive net heating throughout. Unsalted water heats from 20 to x, and the mixture heats from z(x) to B, remaining liquid until each relevant endpoint. Solubility and absence of intermediate phase changes during the instantaneous idealized mixing are independent physical applicability requirements. If the full feasible set is nonempty under these affine constraints it is an interval; L and U should be its endpoints if optimizing over all feasible schedules. A deliberately narrower interval gives an optimum only over that interval. If even immediate mixing is too cold or too hot for these constraints, a conclusion at L=20 is not authorized.

Derived power change, elapsed times, and optimization

Applying the same N to the energy-conserving mixing temperature gives the proved power_change identity:
  N(z(x))-N(x) = k*[S*(x-Ts)+H]/(C+S) = k*D(x)/(C+S).
Since k>0 and C+S>0, net power increases exactly for cooling (D>0), decreases for warming (D<0), and is unchanged for D=0. There are no unrelated before/after powers. A net-power increase alone does not compare heating rates because capacity also changes.

With positive net power, integration of dt/dT=capacity/N(T) gives
  heatingTime(capacity,u,v) = capacity/k * log[N(u)/N(v)].
The Lean definition uses a difference of logarithms; the ratio is dimensionless. All numerical arguments use SI powers and temperatures in C. heating_time_derivative verifies the inverse first-law derivative, and stage_time_from_energy proves that any differentiable inverse elapsed-time curve with this derivative and zero initial value has exactly this endpoint time. This supplies an energy-law derivation and uniqueness, not just arithmetic for an assumed answer.

Total time to salted boiling for addition at x is
  t(x) = heatingTime(C,20,x) + heatingTime(C+S,z(x),B).
Waiting time BEFORE adding salt is heatingTime(C,20,x), not t(x). In particular x=20 gives zero waiting. The proof differentiates the full t, including z'(x)=C/(C+S), obtaining
  t'(x)=C/N(x)-C/N(z(x))
        = C*k*D(x)/[(C+S)*N(x)*N(z(x))].
Thus t' has exactly the sign of D(x), even when S<0. The Mean Value Theorem then proves global comparisons on the feasible interval, rather than just a stationary-point test.

The sole final theorem addition_timing_answer quantifies C,S,H,Ts,B,W,k,A,F,B0,L,U,x, under precisely the displayed feasibility and positivity inequalities and x in [L,U]. Its conclusion is the derived power-jump identity and these five conditional comparisons:

1. If S>=0 and D(L)>=0, then t(L)<=t(x): choose the earliest feasible temperature L.
2. If S>=0 and D(U)<=0, then t(U)<=t(x): choose the latest feasible temperature U.
3. If S>0 and r=Ts-H/S lies in [L,U], then t(r)<=t(x): choose that interior root or endpoint. For S>0 this is equivalently clamping r to [L,U], using cases 1 and 2 when r lies outside.
4. If S<=0, then min(t(L),t(U))<=t(x): compare the two explicit total-time formulas and choose the endpoint with the smaller value. An interior zero of D is a maximum when S<0, not the minimum. The proof handles either sign of D at x and compares along the appropriate subinterval.
5. If S=0 and H=0, then t(L)=t(x): all feasible schedules tie. For S=0,H>0 case 1 chooses earliest; for S=0,H<0 case 2 chooses latest.

These weak inequalities allow ties. They give no numerical time saving or unique optimum. In the distinct lossless limit k=0 all schedules tie in this constant-input calorimetric model, since the required energy C*(B-20)+S*(B-Ts)+H is timing independent. This limit is explanatory and is not a submitted theorem; the logarithmic definitions are used only for k>0.

Compact review packet

Supplied: one litre, 20 C start, pot on stove, unspecified salt and apparatus.
Additional choices: fixed soluble amount/composition/pressure/Ts; uniform pot-water body initially at 20; constant ORIGINAL capacity C>0 and final capacity C+S>0 with signed S; H referenced at Ts; affine enthalpies; shared constant-input Newton-loss law with k>0; instantaneous complete dissolution with no phase/material losses or delays. Feasible domain and positive-power endpoint constraints are explicit above. No empirical sign for S or H is assumed or inferred.
Necessary definitions in Lean: initialTemperature=20; netPower=N; mixedTemperature=z; heatingTime=integrated inverse first law; boilingTime=t. D and r are prose abbreviations only and are expanded in the final theorem. F,B0,L,U are direct scalar binders, not wrapper predicates. There are no additional axioms or sorry. Algebra, trajectory bounds, logarithmic integration and derivative signs are intermediate proved facts, not review assumptions.
Proved conclusion: exactly the power-change identity and five timing regimes listed above, with the stated domain. It is a conditional scientific answer; it does not establish that these approximations fit the actual pot or identify which regime applies. Measurements or literature for specified salt mass, composition, H at Ts and solution heat capacity across the temperature range, together with a calibrated heating curve and pressure, would select and test a regime. Salt temperature and feasible endpoints also matter. A numerical number of seconds requires C,W,k,A and the selected addition temperature; none are supplied. No human acceptance is claimed.

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),
   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The mixing temperature jump and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →
    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu
  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by
    intro g hg
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact le_refl 0
  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,
      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by
    intro y hy
    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))
    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp
  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd
  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by
    intro y hy
    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)
  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by
    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]
  linarith

/- Eliminate the two heating stages. The derivative compares the time
   spent heating unsalted water with the time saved in the salted stage. -/
lemma boiling_time_derivative :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C / netPower W k A x -
       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith [hy.2]

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy

    · intro y hy

   changed heat capacity are both included. -/

       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith [hy.2]

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).neg.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).neg.hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      have hn : C * (k * (S * (y - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
          (netPower W k A y * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) ≤ 0 :=
        div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
          (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hC)
            (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
              (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
          (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr hn
  have hh := hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv
  linarith

/- Conditional scientific answer over an explicitly feasible interval.
   S>=0: earliest, latest, or interior root as D changes sign.
   S<=0: compare endpoint boiling times. S=H=0: all schedules tie.
   H is allowed either sign; mixing need not cool or increase net power. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    x ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ S * (L - Ts) + H →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → S * (U - Ts) + H ≤ 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 < S → Ts - H / S ∈ Set.Icc L U →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A (Ts - H / S) ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S ≤ 0 →
      min (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L) (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U) ≤
        boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S = 0 → H = 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L = boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hx
  have hp : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc L U, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) := by
    intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y
      hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy).2.2
  have inc : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_increasing_on_cooling C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  have dec : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_decreasing_on_warming C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hS hD
    apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hD
    apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  · intro hS hr
    have hroot : S * ((Ts - H / S) - Ts) + H = 0 := by
      field_simp
      <;> ring
    by_cases hxr : x ≤ Ts - H / S
    · apply dec x (Ts - H / S) hx.1 hr.2 hxr
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply inc (Ts - H / S) x hr.1 hx.2 (le_of_not_ge hxr)
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS
    by_cases hD : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H
    · apply le_trans (min_le_left _ _)
      apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply le_trans (min_le_right _ _)
      apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
      intro y hy
      have hh := le_of_not_ge hD
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hH
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
    · apply dec L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]

Supplied information and inference limits

The user supplies one litre of water initially at 20 degrees Celsius, a pot and a stove already heating it, and the intention to add salt. Salt identity, quantity, temperature, pressure, pot, heater and room conditions are unspecified. There are no calorimetric or heating-curve observations. The volume and initial temperature do not identify heat capacities, dissolution energy, heater input, losses, or the final boiling temperature. No exact mass/capacity is invented from the litre. There is no statistical observation model, likelihood or prior: the available inference is deterministic and conditional. No experiment or simulated experiment was performed; no operator response was requested or fabricated; incorporated_inputs is empty.

Physical model and correct capacity meaning

Fix the same soluble salt quantity, salt initial temperature Ts, pressure and final composition across schedules. Treat water and pot as a uniform body initially equilibrated at 20 C. Approximate its capacity C>0 and the final solution-plus-pot capacity C+S>0 as constants over the relevant liquid-temperature range. Here
  C = original water capacity + pot capacity,
  S = final solution capacity - original water capacity.
The pot contribution cancels in S. S is a signed effective capacity difference, NOT the positive capacity of the solid salt. We impose no sign on S. This is the requested conditional-regimes approach, not an assertion of a sign for all NaCl solutions or any other unspecified salt. For a specified solute with amount n, the thermodynamic definition gives S=n*C_app, where C_app is its apparent molar heat capacity at the specified composition and temperature. That apparent capacity is not the solid's molar capacity. A real solution's S(T) can vary with temperature; the constant-capacity approximation must be tested over the heating range.

Partanen & Partanen, Journal of Solution Chemistry 54, 286-316 (2025), Eq. (9), defines C_app as (solution capacity - pure-water capacity)/solute amount. Their analysis treats its composition and temperature dependence and distinguishes real apparent quantities from relative apparent quantities. This supports the capacity interpretation, not a constant value or sign for the user's water. We import no table values or parameter estimates.
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10953-024-01412-5

Dissolution energy reference and mixing balance

H (joules) is the integral isothermal enthalpy of dissolution of the fixed solid salt amount into the fixed water amount at temperature Ts, the ACTUAL initial salt temperature, with the chosen final concentration. Positive H means endothermic at that reference. H can have either sign. It is a fixed reference enthalpy, not a temperature-independent dissolution enthalpy at every addition temperature.

Take the original water-plus-pot enthalpy as zero at Ts and the separate salt's enthalpy as zero at its initial Ts. Under the constant-capacity model, the final solution-plus-pot enthalpy at temperature z is H+(C+S)*(z-Ts). Initial enthalpy just before addition at temperature x is C*(x-Ts). Instantaneous adiabatic mixing/dissolution therefore gives
  H+(C+S)*(z-Ts) = C*(x-Ts),
  z(x) = (C*x+S*Ts-H)/(C+S).
Equivalently, the signed mixing cooling energy is D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H, and z-x=-D(x)/(C+S). Negative D means WARMING on mixing; no cooling premise is used.

For consistency, if the solid salt's constant sensible capacity is cs, isothermal dissolution at x costs H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts). This follows by subtracting the reactant capacity C+cs from product capacity C+S and integrating the enthalpy slope. Warming the solid from Ts to x costs cs*(x-Ts); the sum is H+S*(x-Ts). The Lean lemma reference_consistent_balance proves that the resulting balance (C+S)*(z-x)+cs*(x-Ts)+H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts)=0 is equivalent to the displayed z(x). Thus a positive solid heat capacity does not force S>=0. cs cancels and is not an independent parameter needed by the timing conclusion. These affine enthalpy laws are modeling choices; the algebraic consequence is proved. Temperature-dependent capacities would require integrating their actual functions.

Partanen & Partanen, Journal of Solution Chemistry 52, 1352-1385 (2023), Section 2, treats apparent enthalpy, dissolution and adiabatic temperature changes with explicit reference quantities. It provides general thermodynamic background only, not evidence for this pot's H or an exact constant-capacity law.

Heating law and feasible timing domain

The retained approximation is constant heater-to-body power W and fixed room temperature A, with the SAME Newtonian heat loss k*(T-A) before and after addition, k>0. Hence net power is N(T)=W-k*(T-A). Salt does not change W or k at a common temperature in this approximation. The energy law is capacity*dT/dt=N(T), with capacity C before addition and C+S afterward. This model omits evaporation, radiation beyond the effective linear approximation, changes in heat transfer with concentration, heater feedback, material loss, stirring delay and dissolution delay. Mixing and complete dissolution are instantaneous with no heater pause. These are exposed approximations, not inferred facts about the apparatus.

B0 denotes the unsalted boiling temperature and B the fixed final mixture boiling temperature, both at the chosen pressure. F is a common SAFE liquid lower bound for both compositions over the applicable trajectories (choose it within the liquid region, not below either freezing boundary). L and U bound the interval of feasible addition temperatures. The final theorem requires:
  F <= 20 <= L <= U <= B0;
  F <= z(L) and z(U) <= B;
  N(U)>0 and N(B)>0;
  C>0, C+S>0, k>0.
The assumptions do not allow waiting through unsalted boiling. U=B0 permits adding at its onset, without dwelling there. Similarly z(U)=B permits the final endpoint to occur on mixing, without an intervening boiling/evaporation stage. If strict pre-boiling addition is required and U=B0 is excluded, a latest-endpoint optimum becomes an infimum approached from below, unless a smaller closed operational upper bound is selected.

The lemma feasible_trajectory derives that z is increasing (slope C/(C+S)>0) irrespective of S's sign. Therefore every x in [L,U] satisfies 20<=x<=B0 and F<=z(x)<=B, and both stages have positive net heating throughout. Unsalted water heats from 20 to x, and the mixture heats from z(x) to B, remaining liquid until each relevant endpoint. Solubility and absence of intermediate phase changes during the instantaneous idealized mixing are independent physical applicability requirements. If the full feasible set is nonempty under these affine constraints it is an interval; L and U should be its endpoints if optimizing over all feasible schedules. A deliberately narrower interval gives an optimum only over that interval. If even immediate mixing is too cold or too hot for these constraints, a conclusion at L=20 is not authorized.

Derived power change, elapsed times, and optimization

Applying the same N to the energy-conserving mixing temperature gives the proved power_change identity:
  N(z(x))-N(x) = k*[S*(x-Ts)+H]/(C+S) = k*D(x)/(C+S).
Since k>0 and C+S>0, net power increases exactly for cooling (D>0), decreases for warming (D<0), and is unchanged for D=0. There are no unrelated before/after powers. A net-power increase alone does not compare heating rates because capacity also changes.

With positive net power, integration of dt/dT=capacity/N(T) gives
  heatingTime(capacity,u,v) = capacity/k * log[N(u)/N(v)].
The Lean definition uses a difference of logarithms; the ratio is dimensionless. All numerical arguments use SI powers and temperatures in C. heating_time_derivative verifies the inverse first-law derivative, and stage_time_from_energy proves that any differentiable inverse elapsed-time curve with this derivative and zero initial value has exactly this endpoint time. This supplies an energy-law derivation and uniqueness, not just arithmetic for an assumed answer.

Total time to salted boiling for addition at x is
  t(x) = heatingTime(C,20,x) + heatingTime(C+S,z(x),B).
Waiting time BEFORE adding salt is heatingTime(C,20,x), not t(x). In particular x=20 gives zero waiting. The proof differentiates the full t, including z'(x)=C/(C+S), obtaining
  t'(x)=C/N(x)-C/N(z(x))
        = C*k*D(x)/[(C+S)*N(x)*N(z(x))].
Thus t' has exactly the sign of D(x), even when S<0. The Mean Value Theorem then proves global comparisons on the feasible interval, rather than just a stationary-point test.

The sole final theorem addition_timing_answer quantifies C,S,H,Ts,B,W,k,A,F,B0,L,U,x, under precisely the displayed feasibility and positivity inequalities and x in [L,U]. Its conclusion is the derived power-jump identity and these five conditional comparisons:

1. If S>=0 and D(L)>=0, then t(L)<=t(x): choose the earliest feasible temperature L.
2. If S>=0 and D(U)<=0, then t(U)<=t(x): choose the latest feasible temperature U.
3. If S>0 and r=Ts-H/S lies in [L,U], then t(r)<=t(x): choose that interior root or endpoint. For S>0 this is equivalently clamping r to [L,U], using cases 1 and 2 when r lies outside.
4. If S<=0, then min(t(L),t(U))<=t(x): compare the two explicit total-time formulas and choose the endpoint with the smaller value. An interior zero of D is a maximum when S<0, not the minimum. The proof handles either sign of D at x and compares along the appropriate subinterval.
5. If S=0 and H=0, then t(L)=t(x): all feasible schedules tie. For S=0,H>0 case 1 chooses earliest; for S=0,H<0 case 2 chooses latest.

These weak inequalities allow ties. They give no numerical time saving or unique optimum. In the distinct lossless limit k=0 all schedules tie in this constant-input calorimetric model, since the required energy C*(B-20)+S*(B-Ts)+H is timing independent. This limit is explanatory and is not a submitted theorem; the logarithmic definitions are used only for k>0.

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),
   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The mixing temperature jump and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →
    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu
  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by
    intro g hg
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact le_refl 0
  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,
      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by
    intro y hy
    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))
    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp
  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd
  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by
    intro y hy
    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)
  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by
    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]
  linarith

/- Eliminate the two heating stages. The derivative compares the time
   spent heating unsalted water with the time saved in the salted stage. -/
lemma boiling_time_derivative :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C / netPower W k A x -
       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith [hy.2]

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).neg.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).neg.hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      have hn : C * (k * (S * (y - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
          (netPower W k A y * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) ≤ 0 :=
        div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
          (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hC)
            (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
              (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
          (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr hn
  have hh := hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv
  linarith

/- Conditional scientific answer over an explicitly feasible interval.
   S>=0: earliest, latest, or interior root as D changes sign.
   S<=0: compare endpoint boiling times. S=H=0: all schedules tie.
   H is allowed either sign; mixing need not cool or increase net power. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    x ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ S * (L - Ts) + H →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → S * (U - Ts) + H ≤ 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 < S → Ts - H / S ∈ Set.Icc L U →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A (Ts - H / S) ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S ≤ 0 →
      min (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L) (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U) ≤
        boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S = 0 → H = 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L = boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hx
  have hp : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc L U, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) := by
    intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y
      hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy).2.2
  have inc : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_increasing_on_cooling C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  have dec : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_decreasing_on_warming C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hS hD
    apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hD
    apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  · intro hS hr
    have hroot : S * ((Ts - H / S) - Ts) + H = 0 := by
      field_simp
      <;> ring
    by_cases hxr : x ≤ Ts - H / S
    · apply dec x (Ts - H / S) hx.1 hr.2 hxr
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply inc (Ts - H / S) x hr.1 hx.2 (le_of_not_ge hxr)
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS
    by_cases hD : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H
    · apply le_trans (min_le_left _ _)
      apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply le_trans (min_le_right _ _)
      apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
      intro y hy
      have hh := le_of_not_ge hD
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hH
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
