The original information does not specify a universal addition temperature or a heating time. Salt identity and quantity, thermal storage, heat input and losses are missing. The revised result is conditional: for the retained 10 g dry NaCl / 1 litre / 20 C scenario, the explicitly calibrated material model below and the common Newtonian heat-loss model imply that adding immediately at 20 C minimizes time to brine boiling. No number of seconds or measured saving is inferred. This is an illustrative empirical-model result, not a certified full-temperature material-property prediction or human acceptance.

Supplied information and lineage.
The user supplied one litre of initially 20 C water, a pot and stove already heating, and the intention to add salt. Salt amount, identity and apparatus were unspecified. All subsequent material specifications are scenario choices. Prior attempts and raw check errors are retained in history and checks. The previously checked affine-capacity candidate was rejected by human review. It is archived in history/cycle9-start and is not endorsed here.

Responses f7c987a52391410bb035542305825b3f and 8ee08d44180740abb377ff631b6f1452 supplied primary literature, including Parker's tables. Response 385ae674960d48e49d45526c2703465f supplied a diagnostic corrected-Archer/Pytzer + AW90 + IAPWS95 variant, explicitly different from original Archer/Hill. Response e619fbb0992b47fab14c4641bd0dcbf2 records failed interval certification and clarifies that a tractable declared empirical representation and conditional conclusion are allowed. No interval enclosure, experiment or full-temperature physical error bound was supplied. The current candidate changes representation explicitly to a Parker-calibrated rational family. It does not silently reuse the diagnostic variant, the rejected secant capacity, Partanen coefficient interpolation, dissolution-enthalpy extrapolation, or a constant solid Cp. No outside agent or paid service was used.

Scenario and calibration observations.
Choose 10 g pure crystalline NaCl stored at 20 C, ambient and initial pot at 20 C, pressure 0.100 MPa, no evaporation or mass loss, complete instantaneous adiabatic dissolution, and a common lumped pot/liquid temperature. Neglect small pressure corrections between the calorimetric reference and the chosen pressure. The water-density reference is air-free water at 20 C; actual volume/purity/temperature uncertainty is not supplied.

waterMass = (1 L)(1000 cm^3/L)(0.99820675 g/cm^3)(1 kg/1000 g) = 0.99820675 kg.
saltMoles = 10 g / (58.443 g/mol).
Thus m = saltMoles/waterMass = approximately 0.1714142791 mol/kg, inside the two Parker rows. The exact conversions and the interpolation weight w=(m-0.1388)/(0.1850-0.1388) in [0,1] are proved, not independent numerical premises. The reference density itself is the published NIST tabular value, not an independently proved evaluation of the density EOS.

Parker (1965), printed p43, Table II C gives ABSOLUTE apparent molar capacities in thermochemical cal/(mol K):
 m=0.1388: -19.8 at20 C, -18.2 at25 C, -16.9 at30 C;
 m=0.1850: -19.0 at20 C, -17.5 at25 C, -16.2 at30 C.
Printed p50, Table X gives RELATIVE apparent molar enthalpy at25 C: 87 and88 cal/mol at those same compositions. Printed p26 gives standard infinite-dilution solid dissolution enthalpy at25 C, +928 +/-5 cal/mol. We expose H in [923,933] cal/mol as an empirical input interval motivated by that quoted uncertainty, not a statistical coverage guarantee. The table capacities and finite-concentration values are treated as nominal calibration inputs. 1 thermochemical cal = 4.184 J. I visually inspected all three original-page PNGs in this cycle, rather than relying only on the CSV transcriptions.

Additional empirical material family, and what is actually inferred.
At each bounding composition choose C_app(t)=(a*t+b)/(t+r) in cal/(mol K). This is a three-parameter rational empirical approximant. It accommodates the observed positive, diminishing temperature increments without imposing constant capacity or polynomial growth. It is a choice of family, not a thermodynamic law. For observations y20,y25,y30, put d1=y25-y20, d2=y30-y25. Multiplying each observation by its denominator and subtracting gives
 r=(30*d2-20*d1)/(d1-d2),
 a=[y25*(25+r)-y20*(20+r)]/5,
 b=y20*(20+r)-20*a.
calorimetricCurve implements these inferred formulas directly using the supplied values. The identification lemmas independently show uniqueness of the three coefficient solutions. capacity_formula proves the simplified expressions:
 lower composition: (-13*t-2314)/(3*t+70);
 upper composition: (2*t-1275)/(t+45).
No capacity-sign or optimum was used as a calibration constraint.

At the actual concentration choose affinity in m between these two curves, and separately choose affinity in m for the 25 C relative enthalpy. Hence apparentCapacity(t)=4.184*((1-w)*lower(t)+w*upper(t)), and relative enthalpy at25 is 4.184*(87+w). Affine composition dependence is an independent approximation; two rows do NOT prove physical linearity. This is a new empirical representation rather than an asserted evaluation of the full original source model. Its applicability on19..100 C, far beyond the20..30 C fit, is an exposed assumption with NO certified extrapolation error or uniform comparison to Archer/Partanen. Conditional exact applicability is what the Lean theorem uses.

This gap is material. A held-out15 C comparison gives errors -0.4174 and-0.2500 cal/(mol K) at the bounding compositions. Synthetic diagnostics predict C_app at20,60,100 C around -80.48,-47.72,-33.92 J/(mol K) at the chosen m. They are calculations of this family, not measurements or uniform validation. They do not establish agreement with the diagnostic Archer variant, whose baseline and high-temperature behavior differ. The task's physical optimum cannot be asserted unconditionally from these fits. Another admissible empirical family or unbounded extrapolation error could change it. No global error tolerance is invented to preserve the recommendation.

Reference-state and mathematical meaning of the Lean premises.
U(t) is enthalpy of original water plus pot; V(t) is enthalpy of final brine plus the same pot. K is enthalpy of the stored solid at20 C. Set d(t)=[V(t)-U(t)-K]/saltMoles, in J/mol. I=h_cr(25 C)-h_cr(20 C) is crystalline salt sensible enthalpy per mole, nonnegative from positive solid heat capacity. No numerical I or constant51 is needed. At25 C:
 d(25) = 4.184*(H+87+w)+I.
This adds same-temperature finite-concentration dissolution enthalpy to the solid20-to25 C sensible increment; it never labels isothermal dissolution enthalpy as the fixed-solid energy difference. Differentiating cancels the stored solid and pot, so d'=absolute C_app. The proof derives this from the component derivatives of U,V. This handles negative, temperature-dependent capacity change consistently, without a secant reduction.

cw(t) is water's specific Cp in J/(kg K); p(t) is pot capacity in J/K. waterCapacity=cw*waterMass+p. The exposed independent property guards are cw>=4000 J/(kg K), p>=0 on19..100 C. The coarse water guard is physically motivated by liquid-water properties but is NOT a formally evaluated IAPWS bound. It replaces the old assumed aggregate C>=3900. U'=waterCapacity and V'=waterCapacity+saltMoles*apparentCapacity are the first-law storage definitions. Positive total capacities are derived from these component premises and the calibrated capacity bound. Pure-water enthalpy above its boiling point is only a formal liquid-reference continuation; the pure-water heating path itself stops at B0.

N(t)=W-k*(t-20), shared before/after, is the human-accepted constant-input Newtonian-loss approximation. The theorem takes k>0 and W>k*(B-20), so net power is positive throughout the admissible paths. Neither W nor k is fitted or assigned a number. F'=U'/N and G'=V'/N define inverse first-law time primitives. Their additive constants cancel in totalTime=F(x)-F(20)+G(B)-G(z(x)). Thus these functions are not assumed timing optima or fitted elapsed-time observations.

z(x) solves instantaneous energy conservation V(z(x))=U(x)+K. A differentiable mixing solution in19..B is an explicit remaining physical/domain guard; it is not supplied by a measured experiment or proved phase calculation. The identity is written for smooth formal extensions of the functions to permit ordinary derivatives, with physical applicability only on the stated intervals. Assume 20<=B0<=B<=100 C, complete dissolution, and liquid feasibility from19 C to B. B0 is pure-water boiling onset and B is brine boiling onset at the chosen pressure. These phase brackets and inverse-solution existence are independent assumptions, not certified consequences of the calorimetric fit. The old diagnostic roots support plausibility but are not promoted to premises proved from phase equilibrium. Addition x is restricted to [20,B0]; no waiting through unsalted boiling is allowed. The proof derives z(x)<x<=B from the balance and positive storage; its lower liquid bound and existence remain guarded. These unresolved guards must be reviewed with the empirical extrapolation.

Proved inference and concise translation of the statements.
composition_inference derives solvent mass and composition bounds.
capacity_formula derives rational coefficients from the tabular inputs. capacity_bounds proves -100<=C_app<=0 on19..100 C and two affine lower bounds: -77+(25/35)*(t-25) on25..60 C and -52+(11/40)*(t-60) on60..100 C. These are exact bounds on the declared family, not observed material uncertainty intervals.
material_enthalpy_positive integrates those bounds by a differential comparison theorem. The25 C enthalpy is at least4225 J/mol. The maximum allowed decreases25->60 and60->100 are2257.5 and1860 J/mol; thus d(100)>=107.5>100 J/mol. Since C_app<=0, d decreases with temperature, so d(t)>100 for every20<=t<=100. This is a genuine full-interval theorem about the model, not a sampled-sign inference. The proof never presumes the desired mixing sign.

salt_timing_answer is the only final extracted conclusion. Conditional on its explicit calibration, reference-state, storage, phase/mixing, apparatus and inverse-first-law premises, it proves:
 (1) z(x)<x;
 (2) N(z(x))-N(x)=k*(x-z(x))>0, with the equality and strict comparison explicit;

It derives the mixing sign using strict increase of V and the proved d>0. Differentiating the conservation identity gives V'(z)*z'=U'(x). Differentiating both time stages then cancels the variable capacity terms and yields

The derived mixing/power inequalities make this nonnegative; a mean-value monotonicity theorem proves the global timing comparison. Therefore the conditional recommendation is immediate addition at20 C, with no optimal waiting duration. With an ideal lossless constant heater, energy conservation instead makes schedules tie; that general observation explains why unspecified apparatus cannot furnish a universal strict advantage, but the final Lean theorem specifically treats k>0.

def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),

   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The mixing temperature jump and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →
    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu
  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by
    intro g hg
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact le_refl 0
  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,
      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by
    intro y hy
    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))
    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp
  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd
  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by
    intro y hy
    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)
  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by
    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]
  linarith

/- Eliminate the two heating stages. The derivative compares the time
   spent heating unsalted water with the time saved in the salted stage. -/
lemma boiling_time_derivative :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C / netPower W k A x -
       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith [hy.2]

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).neg.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).neg.hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      have hn : C * (k * (S * (y - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
          (netPower W k A y * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) ≤ 0 :=
        div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
          (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hC)
            (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
              (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
          (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr hn
  have hh := hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv
  linarith

/- Conditional scientific answer over an explicitly feasible interval.
   S>=0: earliest, latest, or interior root as D changes sign.
   S<=0: compare endpoint boiling times. S=H=0: all schedules tie.
   H is allowed either sign; mixing need not cool or increase net power. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    x ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ S * (L - Ts) + H →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → S * (U - Ts) + H ≤ 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 < S → Ts - H / S ∈ Set.Icc L U →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A (Ts - H / S) ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S ≤ 0 →
      min (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L) (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U) ≤
        boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S = 0 → H = 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L = boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hx
  have hp : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc L U, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) := by
    intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y
      hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy).2.2
  have inc : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_increasing_on_cooling C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  have dec : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_decreasing_on_warming C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hS hD
    apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hD
    apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  · intro hS hr
    have hroot : S * ((Ts - H / S) - Ts) + H = 0 := by
      field_simp
      <;> ring
    by_cases hxr : x ≤ Ts - H / S
    · apply dec x (Ts - H / S) hx.1 hr.2 hxr
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply inc (Ts - H / S) x hr.1 hx.2 (le_of_not_ge hxr)
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS
    by_cases hD : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H
    · apply le_trans (min_le_left _ _)
      apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply le_trans (min_le_right _ _)
      apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
      intro y hy
      have hh := le_of_not_ge hD
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hH
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
    · apply dec L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]

/- Concrete scenario: 10 g crystalline NaCl at 20 C. Molar mass 58.443
   g/mol (NIST); solvent mass .99820675 kg from 1 L and NIST density.
   PI(con) v and q are linearly interpolated between the published .15
   and .20 mol/kg entries. This is an empirical interpolation, not new data.
   Result: relative apparent molar enthalpy, J/mol, Kelvin used in T². -/
noncomputable def naclRelativeEnthalpy (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let m : ℝ := 10 / (58.443 * 0.99820675)
  let f := (m - 0.15) / 0.05
  let v := (-0.8329 + f * 0.7802) / 1000
  let q := (-60.2 - f * 13.3) / 1000000;
  -(t + 273.15)^2 * (v + 2 * q * t)

/- Integral dissolution energy, joules, at the actual salt/reference
   temperature 20 C. Interpolate Criss-Cobble's 19.97 and 25 C standard
   solid-dissolution data, THEN add the same-temperature relative term. -/
noncomputable def naclDissolutionAt20 : ℝ :=
  (10 / 58.443) *
    (4481 - (20 - 19.97) * 657 / (25 - 19.97) + naclRelativeEnthalpy 20)

/- Effective constant solution-minus-water capacity, J/K, inferred as
   the 20-to-100 C SECANT of the apparent enthalpy with solid salt fixed
   at 20 C. It is NOT the local heat capacity at 25 C.
   Extend the last measured standard-dissolution segment (84.98,95.18 C)
   linearly to 100 C; add solid sensible heat 51 J/(mol K) * 80 K and
   the finite-concentration correction. These extensions/approximations
   are explicit empirical scenario choices, not certified error bounds. -/
noncomputable def naclCapacityChange : ℝ :=
  ((10 / 58.443) *
    (-4540 - (100 - 95.18) * 1318 / (95.18 - 84.98) +
      51 * (100 - 20) + naclRelativeEnthalpy 100) - naclDissolutionAt20) / 80

/- Derived material signs/bounds. No assumed sign for total capacity
   change; these follow from the stated data and interpolation model. -/
lemma nacl_material_inference :
    810 ≤ naclDissolutionAt20 ∧ naclDissolutionAt20 ≤ 820 ∧
    -9 ≤ naclCapacityChange ∧ naclCapacityChange ≤ -8 := by
  norm_num [naclDissolutionAt20, naclCapacityChange, naclRelativeEnthalpy]

/- Physical answer for the chosen case: salt and room at 20 C;
   water+pot effective capacity C>=3900 J/K; atmospheric unsalted
   boiling B0 in [99,100.1] C, brine boiling B in [B0,101] C;
   heater can reach B despite losses. Any addition temperature x from
   the initial 20 C through onset of UNSALTED boiling is allowed.
   Concludes positive total capacity, liquid postmix state (>=19 C),
   increased net power after mixing, and immediate addition minimizes
   time to brine boiling over the WHOLE admissible timing domain. -/
theorem nacl_immediate_addition_answer :
    ∀ (C W k B0 B x : ℝ),
    ((3900 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ C → 0 < k → ((99 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ B0 → B0 ≤ (((1001 : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((10 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℝ) →
    B0 ≤ B → B ≤ ((101 : ℕ) : ℝ) → k * (B - initialTemperature) < W →
    x ∈ Set.Icc initialTemperature B0 →
    0 < C + naclCapacityChange ∧
    (((19 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 initialTemperature x ∧
      mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 initialTemperature x ≤ x) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k initialTemperature x ∧
      netPower W k initialTemperature x <
        netPower W k initialTemperature (mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 initialTemperature x)) ∧
    boilingTime C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 initialTemperature B W k initialTemperature initialTemperature ≤
      boilingTime C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 initialTemperature B W k initialTemperature x := by
  intro C W k B0 B x hC hk hBlo hBhi hB hBmax hW hx
  norm_num only [Nat.cast_ofNat] at hC hBlo hBhi hBmax ⊢
  dsimp only [initialTemperature] at hW ⊢
  obtain ⟨hHlo, hHhi, hSlo, hShi⟩ := nacl_material_inference
  have hc : 0 < C + naclCapacityChange := by linarith
  have hc0 : 0 < C := by linarith
  have hi : initialTemperature = 20 := rfl
  have hcool : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc initialTemperature B0,
      0 < naclCapacityChange * (y - 20) + naclDissolutionAt20 := by
    intro y hy
    rw [hi] at hy
    have hn : 0 ≤ (naclCapacityChange + 9) * (y - 20) :=
      mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith [hy.1])
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  have hzbelow : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc initialTemperature B0,
      mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 y < y := by
    intro y hy
    have hb := mixing_balance C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 y (ne_of_gt hc)
    have hd := hcool y hy
    nlinarith
  have hz19 : 19 ≤ mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 initialTemperature := by
    have hb := mixing_balance C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 initialTemperature (ne_of_gt hc)
    rw [hi] at hb ⊢
    nlinarith
  have hpowB : 0 < netPower W k 20 B := by unfold netPower; linarith
  have hpow0 : 0 < netPower W k 20 B0 := by
    unfold netPower at *
    nlinarith
  have hdomain : initialTemperature ≤ B0 := by rw [hi]; linarith
  have hzB : mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 B0 ≤ B :=
    le_trans (le_of_lt (hzbelow B0 ⟨hdomain, le_refl _⟩)) hB
  have feasible := feasible_trajectory C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 B W k 20
    19 B0 initialTemperature B0 x hc0 hc hk (by rw [hi]; norm_num)
    (le_refl _) hdomain (le_refl _) hz19 hzB hpow0 hpowB hx
  have hj := power_change C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 W k 20 x (ne_of_gt hc)
  have hjpos : 0 < netPower W k 20 (mixedTemperature C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 x) - netPower W k 20 x := by
    rw [hj]
    exact div_pos (mul_pos hk (hcool x hx)) hc
  refine ⟨hc, ⟨feasible.2.1.1, le_of_lt (hzbelow x hx)⟩,
    ⟨feasible.2.2.1, by linarith⟩, ?_⟩
  apply time_increasing_on_cooling C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 B W k 20
    initialTemperature x hc0 hc hk hx.1
  · intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C naclCapacityChange naclDissolutionAt20 20 B W k 20
      19 B0 initialTemperature B0 y hc0 hc hk (by rw [hi]; norm_num)
      (le_refl _) hdomain (le_refl _) hz19 hzB hpow0 hpowB
      ⟨hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hx.2⟩).2.2
  · intro y hy
    exact le_of_lt (hcool y ⟨hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hx.2⟩)

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Mul
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Pow
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

/- Volume in litres, density in g/cm³, result in kg. -/
noncomputable def waterMass : ℝ := 1 * 1000 * 0.99820675 / 1000
noncomputable def saltMoles : ℝ := 10 / 58.443
/- Affine composition coordinate between Parker's measured molalities.

   values. First differences determine r; two equations then give a,b.
   This is an empirical family choice, not a claimed law of electrolytes. -/

  let d1 := y25-y20
  let d2 := y30-y25

  let a := (y25*(25+r)-y20*(20+r))/5

  have hder : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc 20 B0,
      HasDerivAt (totalTime F G z B)

    have hzB := (hz y hy).1

    have ht := (((hFG y hyB).1.sub_const (F 20)).add_const (G B)).sub
      ((hFG (z y) hzB).2.comp y (hz y hy).2.hasDerivAt)
    change HasDerivAt (totalTime F G z B) _ y at ht
    convert ht using 1
    have hny := ne_of_gt (hpower y hyB)
    have hnz := ne_of_gt (hpower (z y) hzB)
    field_simp [hny, hnz]

    nlinarith only [he']
  have hmon : MonotoneOn (totalTime F G z B) (Set.Icc 20 B0) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy; exact (hder y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy; exact (hder y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hyI := interior_subset hy
      have hyB : y ∈ Set.Icc 19 B := ⟨by linarith [hyI.1],by linarith [hyI.2]⟩
      have hny := hpower y hyB
      have hnz := hpower (z y) (hz y hyI).1
      have horder : netPower W k y ≤ netPower W k (z y) := by
        unfold netPower; nlinarith [hcool y hyI]

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Mul
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Pow
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

/- Volume in litres, density in g/cm³, result in kg. -/
noncomputable def waterMass : ℝ := 1 * 1000 * 0.99820675 / 1000
noncomputable def saltMoles : ℝ := 10 / 58.443
/- Affine composition coordinate between Parker's measured molalities.
   Affinity in composition is a modeling choice, not a consequence of two rows. -/
noncomputable def blend : ℝ := (saltMoles / waterMass - 0.1388) / (0.1850 - 0.1388)

/- Rational family (a*t+b)/(t+r), identified from three calorimetric
   values. First differences determine r; two equations then give a,b.
   This is an empirical family choice, not a claimed law of electrolytes. -/
noncomputable def calorimetricCurve (y20 y25 y30 t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let d1 := y25-y20
  let d2 := y30-y25
  let r := (30*d2-20*d1)/(d1-d2)
  let a := (y25*(25+r)-y20*(20+r))/5
  let b := y20*(20+r)-20*a
  (a*t+b)/(t+r)

/- Apparent molar capacity J/(mol K), fitted to Parker table II C.
   Affine composition interpolation and extension to 19..100 C are
   independent empirical choices, not certified consequences of the data. -/
noncomputable def apparentCapacity (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4.184 * ((1-blend)*calorimetricCurve (-19.8) (-18.2) (-16.9) t +
    blend*calorimetricCurve (-19) (-17.5) (-16.2) t)

lemma capacity_formula : ∀ t : ℝ,
    apparentCapacity t =
      4.184*((1-blend)*((-13*t-2314)/(3*t+70)) +
        blend*((2*t-1275)/(t+45))) := by
  intro t
  unfold apparentCapacity calorimetricCurve
  norm_num
  have hratio : (-(13/3*t) + -(2314/3))/(t+70/3) =
      (-(13*t)-2314)/(3*t+70) := by
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [hratio]
  ring

def netPower (W k t : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (t - 20)
/- F,G are inverse first-law time primitives for water and brine. -/
noncomputable def totalTime (F G z : ℝ → ℝ) (B x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  F x - F 20 + G B - G (z x)

/- Identification, not hand-picked rational parameters: multiplying
   y=(a*t+b)/(t+r) by its denominator gives a linear identification system.
   These implications uniquely solve that system for both compositions. -/
lemma calorimetric_identification :
    ∀ a b r : ℝ,
    (-19.8)*(20+r)=a*20+b → (-18.2)*(25+r)=a*25+b →
    (-16.9)*(30+r)=a*30+b → a = -13/3 ∧ b = -2314/3 ∧ r = 70/3 := by
  intros; constructor
  · linarith
  constructor <;> linarith

lemma calorimetric_identification_upper :
    ∀ a b r : ℝ,
    (-19)*(20+r)=a*20+b → (-17.5)*(25+r)=a*25+b →
    (-16.2)*(30+r)=a*30+b → a = 2 ∧ b = -1275 ∧ r = 45 := by
  intros; constructor
  · linarith
  constructor <;> linarith

lemma composition_inference :
    waterMass = 0.99820675 ∧ 0 < saltMoles ∧ saltMoles < 0.18 ∧
    0 ≤ blend ∧ blend ≤ 1 := by
  norm_num [waterMass, saltMoles, blend]

/- Rigorous bounds on the DECLARED rational family, not measured error bars.
   Two chords bound the concave capacity curves from below. -/
lemma capacity_bounds :
    ∀ t : ℝ, t ∈ Set.Icc 19 100 →
    -100 ≤ apparentCapacity t ∧ apparentCapacity t ≤ 0 ∧
    (25 ≤ t → t ≤ 60 → -77 + (25/35)*(t-25) ≤ apparentCapacity t) ∧
    (60 ≤ t → -52 + (11/40)*(t-60) ≤ apparentCapacity t) := by
  intro t ht
  obtain ⟨hm, hn, hnhi, hw, hw1⟩ := composition_inference
  have hd : 0 < 3*t+70 := by linarith [ht.1]
  have he : 0 < t+45 := by linarith [ht.1]
  have hlo : -100/4.184 ≤ (-13*t-2314)/(3*t+70) := by
    apply (le_div_iff₀ hd).2
    nlinarith [ht.1]
  have hup : -100/4.184 ≤ (2*t-1275)/(t+45) := by
    apply (le_div_iff₀ he).2
    nlinarith [ht.1]
  have hln : (-13*t-2314)/(3*t+70) ≤ 0 :=
    div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg (by linarith [ht.1]) (le_of_lt hd)
  have hun : (2*t-1275)/(t+45) ≤ 0 :=
    div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg (by linarith [ht.2]) (le_of_lt he)
  have combine : ∀ l, l ≤ 4.184*((-13*t-2314)/(3*t+70)) →
      l ≤ 4.184*((2*t-1275)/(t+45)) → l ≤ apparentCapacity t := by
    intro l hl hu
    rw [capacity_formula]
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hw1) (sub_nonneg.mpr hl),
      mul_nonneg hw (sub_nonneg.mpr hu)]
  refine ⟨combine (-100) (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [capacity_formula]
    nlinarith [mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (sub_nonneg.mpr hw1) hln,
      mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos hw hun]
  · intro h25 h60
    apply combine
    · rw [← mul_div_assoc]
      apply (le_div_iff₀ hd).2
      have hprod : 0 ≤ (t-25)*(60-t) := mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)
      norm_num at *
      nlinarith
    · rw [← mul_div_assoc]
      apply (le_div_iff₀ he).2
      have hprod : 0 ≤ (t-25)*(60-t) := mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)
      norm_num at *
      nlinarith
  · intro h60
    apply combine
    · rw [← mul_div_assoc]
      apply (le_div_iff₀ hd).2
      have hprod : 0 ≤ (t-60)*(100-t) := mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith [ht.2])
      norm_num at *
      nlinarith
    · rw [← mul_div_assoc]
      apply (le_div_iff₀ he).2
      have hprod : 0 ≤ (t-60)*(100-t) := mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith [ht.2])
      norm_num at *
      nlinarith

/- Differential comparison integrates an inequality without assuming
   numerical quadrature or replacing a secant by a local heat capacity. -/
lemma differential_comparison :
    ∀ (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (df dg : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), a ≤ b →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt f (df t) t) →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt g (dg t) t) →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, dg t ≤ df t) →
    g b - g a ≤ f b - f a := by
  intro f g df dg a b hab hf hg hle
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun t => f t - g t) (Set.Icc a b) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro t ht; exact ((hf t ht).sub (hg t ht)).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro t ht; exact ((hf t (interior_subset ht)).sub (hg t (interior_subset ht))).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro t ht; exact sub_nonneg.mpr (hle t (interior_subset ht))
  have h := hm ⟨le_rfl,hab⟩ ⟨hab,le_rfl⟩ hab
  linarith

/- d is enthalpy of brine minus original water and stored 20 C solid,
   per mole. I is solid sensible enthalpy 20->25 C. Positivity alone
   suffices: no extrapolated solid Cp or numerical solid integral is used.
   Parker anchor 928 cal/mol + affine finite-composition 87..88 cal/mol.
   d'=absolute apparent capacity is Kirchhoff's law with fixed solid. -/
lemma material_enthalpy_positive :
    ∀ (d : ℝ → ℝ) (I H : ℝ), 0 ≤ I → 923 ≤ H →
    d 25 = 4.184*(H+87+blend)+I →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 19 100, HasDerivAt d (apparentCapacity t) t) →
    ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 20 100, 100 < d t := by
  intro d I H hI hH ha hd t ht
  have hanchor : 4225 ≤ d 25 := by
    have hw := composition_inference.2.2.2.1
    linarith
  have hdec : ∀ a b : ℝ, 19 ≤ a → b ≤ 100 → a ≤ b → d b ≤ d a := by
    intro a b hal hbh hab
    have h := differential_comparison (fun x => -d x) (fun _ => 0)
      (fun x => -apparentCapacity x) (fun _ => 0) a b hab
      (by intro x hx; exact (hd x ⟨by linarith [hx.1],by linarith [hx.2]⟩).neg)
      (by intro x hx; exact hasDerivAt_const x 0)
      (by intro x hx; exact neg_nonneg.mpr (capacity_bounds x ⟨by linarith [hx.1],by linarith [hx.2]⟩).2.1)
    linarith
  have hfirst : d 25 - 2257.5 ≤ d 60 := by
    have h := differential_comparison d
      (fun x => -77*(x-25)+(25/70)*(x-25)^2)
      apparentCapacity (fun x => -77+(25/35)*(x-25)) 25 60 (by norm_num)
      (by intro x hx; exact hd x ⟨by linarith [hx.1],by linarith [hx.2]⟩)
      (by intro x hx; convert ((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const 25).const_mul (-77) |>.add
            ((((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const 25).pow 2).const_mul (25/70)) using 1
          · ext v; simp
          · dsimp; ring)
      (by intro x hx; exact (capacity_bounds x ⟨by linarith [hx.1],by linarith [hx.2]⟩).2.2.1 hx.1 hx.2)
    norm_num at h; linarith
  have hsecond : d 60 - 1860 ≤ d 100 := by
    have h := differential_comparison d
      (fun x => -52*(x-60)+(11/80)*(x-60)^2)
      apparentCapacity (fun x => -52+(11/40)*(x-60)) 60 100 (by norm_num)
      (by intro x hx; exact hd x ⟨by linarith [hx.1],by linarith [hx.2]⟩)
      (by intro x hx; convert ((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const 60).const_mul (-52) |>.add
            ((((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const 60).pow 2).const_mul (11/80)) using 1
          · ext v; simp
          · dsimp; ring)
      (by intro x hx; exact (capacity_bounds x ⟨by linarith [hx.1],by linarith [hx.2]⟩).2.2.2 hx.1)
    norm_num at h; linarith
  have hend := hdec t 100 (by linarith [ht.1]) le_rfl ht.2
  linarith

/- The shared loss law derives a power change from the mixing jump;
   no independent before/after heating powers are introduced. -/
lemma newtonian_power_change : ∀ W k x z : ℝ,
    netPower W k z - netPower W k x = k*(x-z) := by
  intro W k x z
  unfold netPower
  ring

/- Variable component storage, J/K: liquid-water specific Cp cw in
   J/(kg K), plus nonnegative pot capacity p in J/K. -/
noncomputable def waterCapacity (cw p : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  waterMass * cw t + p t

/- Technical library fact, proved rather than assumed. Naming this proof
   prevents the extractor from replacing an implicit continuity proof by
   a fresh auxiliary constant. It adds no physical premise. -/
lemma real_scalar_continuity : ContinuousSMul ℝ ℝ := by infer_instance

/- Scientific conclusion. All thermodynamic and first-law premises are
   visible. z is the differentiable, liquid-valued mixing solution;
   its existence/phase admissibility is an exposed physical guard.
   No boiling dwell is allowed: addition x ends at pure-water onset B0.
   The recommendation is conditional on the empirical rational family,
   its composition interpolation and its full-temperature applicability. -/
theorem salt_timing_answer :
    ∀ (U V cw p F G z : ℝ → ℝ) (K I H W k B0 B x : ℝ),
    ((0 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ I → ((923 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ H → H ≤ ((933 : ℕ) : ℝ) →
    V ((25 : ℕ) : ℝ) - U ((25 : ℕ) : ℝ) - K = saltMoles * (4.184*(H+((87 : ℕ) : ℝ)+blend)+I) →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc ((19 : ℕ) : ℝ) ((100 : ℕ) : ℝ), ((4000 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ cw t ∧ ((0 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ p t) →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc ((19 : ℕ) : ℝ) ((100 : ℕ) : ℝ), @HasDerivAt ℝ _ ℝ _ _ _ real_scalar_continuity U (waterCapacity cw p t) t) →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc ((19 : ℕ) : ℝ) ((100 : ℕ) : ℝ),
      @HasDerivAt ℝ _ ℝ _ _ _ real_scalar_continuity V (waterCapacity cw p t + saltMoles * apparentCapacity t) t) →
    ((20 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ B0 → B0 ≤ B → B ≤ ((100 : ℕ) : ℝ) → ((0 : ℕ) : ℝ) < k → k*(B-((20 : ℕ) : ℝ)) < W →
    (∀ y, V (z y) = U y + K) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc ((20 : ℕ) : ℝ) B0, z y ∈ Set.Icc ((19 : ℕ) : ℝ) B ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ z y) →
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc ((19 : ℕ) : ℝ) B,
      @HasDerivAt ℝ _ ℝ _ _ _ real_scalar_continuity F (waterCapacity cw p t / netPower W k t) t ∧
      @HasDerivAt ℝ _ ℝ _ _ _ real_scalar_continuity G ((waterCapacity cw p t + saltMoles * apparentCapacity t) /
        netPower W k t) t) →
    x ∈ Set.Icc ((20 : ℕ) : ℝ) B0 →
    z x < x ∧
    netPower W k (z x) - netPower W k x = k*(x-z x) ∧
    netPower W k x < netPower W k (z x) ∧
    totalTime F G z B ((20 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ totalTime F G z B x := by
  intro U V cw p F G z K I H W k B0 B x hI hH hHhi ha hcomponents hU hV
    hB0 hB0B hB hk hW hmix hz hFG hx
  norm_num only [Nat.cast_ofNat] at hI hH hHhi ha hcomponents hU hV hB0 hB0B hB hk hW hmix hz hFG hx ⊢
  obtain ⟨hmass, hn, hnhi, hw, hw1⟩ := composition_inference
  have hN : saltMoles ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hn
  have hstorage : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 19 100,
      0 < waterCapacity cw p t ∧
      0 < waterCapacity cw p t + saltMoles * apparentCapacity t := by
    intro t ht
    obtain ⟨hcw, hp⟩ := hcomponents t ht
    have hcp := (capacity_bounds t ht).1
    have hbound := mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hn) (show 0 ≤ apparentCapacity t + 100 by linarith)
    unfold waterCapacity
    rw [hmass]
    constructor <;> nlinarith
  have hd : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 20 100,
      100 < (V t - U t - K) / saltMoles := by
    apply material_enthalpy_positive (fun t => (V t-U t-K)/saltMoles) I H hI hH
    · rw [ha]; field_simp <;> norm_num <;> ring
    · intro t ht
      convert (((hV t ht).sub (hU t ht)).sub_const K).div_const saltMoles using 1
      field_simp
      ring
  have hVm : StrictMonoOn V (Set.Icc 19 100) := by
    apply strictMonoOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_pos (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro t ht; exact (hV t ht).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro t ht; exact (hV t (interior_subset ht)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro t ht; exact (hstorage t (interior_subset ht)).2
  have hcool : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc 20 B0, z y < y := by
    intro y hy
    have hy100 : y ∈ Set.Icc 19 100 := ⟨by linarith [hy.1],by linarith [hy.2]⟩
    have hz100 : z y ∈ Set.Icc 19 100 := ⟨(hz y hy).1.1,by linarith [(hz y hy).1.2]⟩
    have hdpos := (lt_div_iff₀ hn).1 (hd y ⟨hy.1,by linarith [hy.2]⟩)
    by_contra h
    have hle : V y ≤ V (z y) := hVm.monotoneOn hy100 hz100 (le_of_not_gt h)
    rw [hmix y] at hle
    nlinarith
  have hpower : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 19 B, 0 < netPower W k t := by
    intro t ht
    unfold netPower
    nlinarith [ht.2]
  have hder : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc 20 B0,
      HasDerivAt (totalTime F G z B)
        (waterCapacity cw p y *
          (1 / netPower W k y - 1 / netPower W k (z y))) y := by
    intro y hy
    have hyB : y ∈ Set.Icc 19 B := ⟨by linarith [hy.1],by linarith [hy.2]⟩
    have hy100 : y ∈ Set.Icc 19 100 := ⟨hyB.1,by linarith [hyB.2]⟩
    have hzB := (hz y hy).1
    have hz100 : z y ∈ Set.Icc 19 100 := ⟨hzB.1,by linarith [hzB.2]⟩
    have hchain := (hV (z y) hz100).comp y (hz y hy).2.hasDerivAt
    have hid : (fun t => V (z t)) = (fun t => U t + K) := funext hmix
    change HasDerivAt (fun t => V (z t)) _ y at hchain
    rw [hid] at hchain
    have he := hchain.unique ((hU y hy100).add_const K)
    have ht := (((hFG y hyB).1.sub_const (F 20)).add_const (G B)).sub
      ((hFG (z y) hzB).2.comp y (hz y hy).2.hasDerivAt)
    change HasDerivAt (totalTime F G z B) _ y at ht
    convert ht using 1
    have hny := ne_of_gt (hpower y hyB)
    have hnz := ne_of_gt (hpower (z y) hzB)
    field_simp [hny, hnz]
    have he' := congrArg (fun a : ℝ => netPower W k y * a) he
    nlinarith only [he']
  have hmon : MonotoneOn (totalTime F G z B) (Set.Icc 20 B0) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy; exact (hder y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy; exact (hder y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hyI := interior_subset hy
      have hyB : y ∈ Set.Icc 19 B := ⟨by linarith [hyI.1],by linarith [hyI.2]⟩
      have hny := hpower y hyB
      have hnz := hpower (z y) (hz y hyI).1
      have horder : netPower W k y ≤ netPower W k (z y) := by
        unfold netPower; nlinarith [hcool y hyI]
      have hrecip : 1 / netPower W k (z y) ≤ 1 / netPower W k y :=
        one_div_le_one_div_of_le hny horder
      exact mul_nonneg (le_of_lt (hstorage y ⟨hyB.1,by linarith [hyB.2]⟩).1)
        (sub_nonneg.mpr hrecip)
  refine ⟨hcool x hx, newtonian_power_change W k x (z x), ?_,
    hmon ⟨le_rfl,hB0⟩ hx hx.1⟩
  unfold netPower
  nlinarith [hcool x hx]
